gardener_move.rationale: Eval metrics are None (no signal), so make a low-risk deterministic improvement: append a deeper tree_d6 trained on the train split. It only votes on states where shallower trees disagree or err, increasing coverage of optimal moves without adding noisy nondeterministic voters.
The current three-tree majority lets the shallower d3/d4 trees outvote the deeper model. Wiring to tree_d6 alone should reduce dilution from underfit voters.

Adding shallower trees as diversity voters lets MajorityVote smooth out depth-6 overfitting; ties break to lowest move index (tree_d6 first), so strong members retain priority while d4/d3 supply ensemble correction on the frozen eval.

The composition skips depth 5. A train-split depth-5 tree should align more closely with the stronger deeper cells than tree_d3 while adding useful diversity, strengthening the majority without discarding existing coverage.
Append another max-depth tree to increase the influence of the strongest depth family while retaining the existing deeper-tree diversity and reducing tie-prone even-vote outcomes.
Prune the shallow d3/d4 voters that can form a low-depth bloc against the stronger depth-6 trees, while retaining d5 as a tie-breaking third vote.

tree_d6 and tree_d6#2 are identically trained, so they always vote together and form a locked majority; tree_d5's vote is never decisive. Retiring it is a no-risk simplification. The alternatives (adding ollama cells or pinch) would inject noisy third votes that could flip otherwise-correct d6 majorities, and another d6 clone would leave behavior identical.
Add pinch as a third voter to break 1-1 splits between the depth-6 trees; it should not override agreement between the stronger trees and is likely to help on tactical states.
Add a third max-depth tree to reduce vote variance and reinforce the strongest policy family while keeping pinch as the specialist.

Three identical-depth tree_d6 votes are highly correlated, so the ensemble is effectively tree_d6 vs pinch. Appending a tree_d5 adds a decorrelated, deterministic voter trained on the same split; at depth 5 it should agree with tree_d6 on easy states but split on others, breaking deadlocks toward optimal moves and lifting top1_in_optimal off the 0.745 plateau.

Eval has plateaued with three identical tree_d6 clones dominating every vote, making pinch's signal irrelevant (3-1 whenever they disagree). Adding a tree_d5 with a different inductive bias gives a diversity break: in states where d6 trees err, pinch + d5 can form a 2-2 tie that falls to the lowest move index, and in states where the deep trees overfit, d5+pinch can win 2-3 only if one d6 abstains or they split. Low-risk append, modest expected set_recall gain.
Append another maximum-depth tree to reinforce the strongest format-reliable voters and reduce tie/abstention noise from the shallower tree and pinch.

The four tree_d6 clones already form a stable majority; the shallower tree_d5#2 and pinch add vote noise without helping on the frozen eval (metrics flat ~0.745). Removing them makes the ensemble a clean unanimous tree_d6 vote, which should match or slightly exceed the current top1_in_optimal by eliminating dissenting votes on borderline states.

Quick-evals are flat across 5 moves, indicating the four depth-6 trees are highly correlated and plateaued. Appending shallower trees (tree_d5, tree_d4) adds ensemble diversity at low risk: the d6 quartet still dominates most votes, but when a d6 cell abstains or splits, the varied-depth members can shift ties toward optimal moves. Ties already break to lowest move index, so ordering preserves current behavior as a baseline.

Metrics are flat/slightly declining; replacing the weakest member (tree_d4) with an additional depth-5 tree should improve vote quality while adding diversity beyond a fourth d5-equivalent tie bloc, with no format-gate risk since trees always vote.

Metrics are flat at 0.745 top1 with slight set_recall drift; the two depth-5 trees are the weakest voters in the ordered list and likely dilute the depth-6 consensus. Retiring them yields a homogeneous depth-6 committee, reducing variance without changing tie-break semantics.
The all-depth-6 bloc has plateaued. Appending an existing depth-5 tree preserves the depth-6 majority while adding a conservative diversity/tie-breaking voter.

Performance has plateaued with the current d6-heavy ensemble. Adding another independent maximum-depth tree preserves the dominant strong cohort while reducing variance and limiting the influence of the shallower d5 vote.

Adding a shallower tree_d4 diversifies the vote pool: on states where deep trees overfit in a correlated way, tree_d4 can shift the majority toward a different (potentially optimal) move; ties still break to lowest move index. Worst case it's outvoted 6-1 on most states, so downside risk is bounded.
Replace the weakest depth-4 voter with the unused second depth-5 tree, preserving an odd seven-member committee while increasing average capacity and retaining mid-depth diversity.

The plateau is already driven by depth-6 trees; appending another depth-6 learner adds same-capacity ensemble diversity without diluting the vote with weaker shallow or untrusted cells.
